name: Tilda Frey
storeExitText: Come back when you've thought of the thing you forgot. Everyone does.

start.npcText: You'll be the one from the hill. I know every face that comes through that door and I didn't know yours, so it had to be you. Tilda Frey. What are you short of?

responses.text: Where does it all come from?
Who should I know in Hollowbrook?

closed.npcText: The shutters are down, which is the whole of my answer. Come in the morning. And come with a list — you'll spend less, and I'll still make my margin, and we'll both feel clever.

where_from.npcText: The carters, mostly. They stop here because I feed them and don't haggle in front of their apprentices. Alder meets them at the crossroads with the handcart — nineteen and built like a door, that boy, it's the one thing his father left him.

carter_news.npcText: They bring rumor, which is news that hasn't paid for itself yet. Roads are worse east of the ridge. Something's been at the sheep two valleys over — Orik will tell you it's wolves, and Orik has said wolves every year since I was a girl.

responses.text: And what do you think it is?

what_she_thinks.npcText: I think a shepherd who cries wolf every year is right eventually, and I think I'd rather sell lanterns before that than after. Make of that what you like.

alone.npcText: Since the fever, yes — six years now. Alder hauls and Sable keeps the ledger better than I do, and neither of them will thank me for saying so in front of a stranger.

sorry.npcText: That's kind, and you needn't be — it was a long time ago and the shop stayed open, which was the part I was frightened of. Ask Sable about the ledger. She'll show you. She's been waiting years for someone to ask.

who_to_know.npcText: Halda Fenwick, on the forge lane — old as the hill and forgets nothing, which is a rarer combination than people think. She'll want to talk about your family, and you should let her. Beyond that: Bramm pours honest measures, and the reeve means well at volume.

why_family.npcText: Because she was a girl when that museum had queues. Actual queues, down the hill and round the crossroads — I've heard it a hundred times and I still can't picture it. She can. Go and let her.
